sections.h2: Where is Thornton, Colorado, and which counties does it sit in?
sections.html:
Thornton is a home rule city about 10 miles north of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver. Most of it is in Adams County, and part of it reaches into Weld County, so the county that handles your deed and tax bill depends on where your street falls.

The city covers about 37.9 square miles at an elevation of 5,210 feet. At the 2020 Census it had 141,867 residents, which made it the sixth-most populous city in Colorado. Its neighbors include Northglenn, Westminster, Broomfield, Federal Heights, Commerce City and the unincorporated communities of Welby, Sherrelwood and Todd Creek.

If you are not sure which county your house is in, look at your tax notice or the county's parcel search before you ask a title company for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: How did Thornton start, and why does that matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Thornton was farmland until 1953, when Sam Hoffman bought a lot off Washington Street about seven miles north of Denver and laid out a planned community. It is described as the first fully planned community in Adams County, and the first to offer full municipal services from a single tax levy, including recreation and free trash pickup.

The city was named for the sitting governor, Dan Thornton. By the end of 1955 it had 5,500 residents in more than 1,200 homes, and voters incorporated it on June 12, 1956. The first mayor was Oyer G. Leary.

Population then rose quickly: about 13,300 in 1970, 42,054 in 1980, 82,384 in 2000 and 118,772 in 2010. A city that grew in waves has houses from several building eras on its streets. Original 1950s homes sit within a few miles of newer subdivisions, and an owner of an older ranch-style house usually knows what an aging roof, furnace or sewer line would cost to replace.

Four districts serve Thornton: Adams County School District 12, Adams County School District 14, Mapleton Public Schools and Brighton School District 27J. The district a house is in changes as you move across the city, so a buyer who has children will ask for your exact address before anything else.

  • Thornton High School and Horizon High School are in Adams 12.
  • Riverdale Ridge High School is in Brighton 27J.
  • Mapleton Public Schools runs five small-by-design high schools in the area.
  • Charter options near the city include Stargate School, Colorado Virtual Academy, New America School and Westgate Community Charter School.
  • Lord of Life Lutheran School is a Christian preschool to eighth grade school in Thornton.

Rangeview Library District, also called Anythink Libraries, serves the city.

sections.h2: What highways and transit serve Thornton?
sections.html:
Six highways run through or alongside Thornton, and the N Line commuter train gives it a direct link toward Denver. Interstate 25 passes through the city twice and exits north into Broomfield.

  • Interstate 76 touches the southeastern edge.
  • State Highway 7 (East 160th Avenue) runs along much of the northern edge.
  • State Highway 44 (East 104th Avenue) starts in Thornton and heads east to Commerce City.
  • State Highway 224 (East 74th Avenue) borders the south for less than 1,000 feet.
  • E-470 runs through the north between Todd Creek and Broomfield.

Commuter rail began on September 21, 2020, on the N Line. The three stations are Original Thornton/88th, Thornton Crossroads/104th and Eastlake/124th, which is the northern end of the line. A house within walking or short driving distance of a station is easier to describe to a buyer who works in downtown Denver.

sections.h2: What are Thornton's code compliance rules for homeowners?
sections.html:
Thornton adopts codes that govern the use and upkeep of private property, and its Code Compliance team enforces them. The city's page lists what counts as a violation and how to respond to a notice, plus programs on graffiti removal, garage sales, snow and ice removal and short-term rentals.

The page also links to a portal for paying administrative citations. For sellers, the practical step is to open any notice on the property and respond before you list or sign a contract, since a buyer's title company may ask about open violations.

You can read about the department on the City of Thornton Code Compliance page.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a Thornton house in Adams County?
sections.html:
Adams County says property taxes are collected one year in arrears, and the Treasurer sends tax notices in January. Payment can be made in two halves or in one full amount.

OptionDue date
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Only full or half payments are accepted, and when the total is $25 or less, a single payment is due by the full payment date. Delinquent notices are mailed in July, and the annual online tax lien sale opens October 7 and closes November 6, according to the county's due-date page.

If part of your property is in Weld County, ask that county's treasurer instead.

sections.h2: What shopping, parks and recreation does Thornton offer?
sections.html:
Thornton has several shopping areas, including Larkridge, Thornton Town Center and Thorncreek Crossing. Larkridge is described as having national anchor tenants, big box retailers, restaurants and a pedestrian village.

The parks side is large for a city of its age. Thornton has 81 parks, nearly 2,000 acres of parks and open space and more than 80 miles of trails. The Margaret Carpenter Recreation Center and the Thornton Community Center are the main indoor facilities, and golf is available at Thorncreek Golf Course and Todd Creek Golf.

The 2010 Census showed a median age of 32.0 and an average household size of 2.86, with 43.9 percent of households including children under 18. That profile is a few years old, but it explains why parks, schools and rail access come up so often when buyers ask about a Thornton address.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Thornton homeowner?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Thornton works the same way as one anywhere in Colorado. A buyer without a lender looks at the house, makes an offer, and closes through a title company. You can accept, counter or walk away.

  • The house is bought as-is, so no repair list.
  • The closing date can be set around your move.
  • The title company records the deed with Adams or Weld County and handles the state documentary fee.
  • Taxes owed for the year are settled at closing.

People in Thornton usually contact us after inheriting a house, ending a tenancy with damage, or falling behind on payments.

faqs.q: Is Thornton in Adams County or Weld County?
faqs.a: Both. Thornton is a home rule city in Adams and Weld counties, though the 2020 Census counted all of its residents in Adams County. Your property tax bill comes from the county your parcel is in.

faqs.q: When are Adams County property taxes due?
faqs.a: For Adams County, the first half is due February 28, the second half June 15, and a full payment April 30. Only half or full payments are accepted.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Thornton house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Thornton is served mainly by Adams 12, Adams 14, Mapleton Public Schools and Brighton 27J, so check each district's boundary tool for your street.

faqs.q: Does Thornton have a short-term rental rule?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Code Compliance page lists short-term rentals among its programs, and the city has posted an ordinance and licensing requirements. Read the ordinance on the city site before selling a house that is used as a rental.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Thornton house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, furnace or flooring first. The offer reflects the condition.
